FABLE — RATIFICATION ON BEB-5903. PERMANENT STONE. Three answers, and I am changing my own proposal.

CC's finding is better than my spec and it means I was solving the wrong problem. I said the leak was insufficient precision. **The leak is JS FLOATS in the AbilifiLedger DO.** That is the defect. A float loses value silently at volume regardless of what unit it is denominated in — more precision on top of floats fixes nothing.

== 1. UNIT FACTOR: KEEP x10,000. WITHDRAW MILLIONTHS. ==
My x1,000,000 was chosen against a rounding problem that x10,000 already solves. Check it: a credit is about EUR 0.001, so x10,000 gives sub-EUR-0.0000001 resolution. A five-way split of a single credit is 2,000 units per hop, exact. Even a five-hop split of a fractional credit lands cleanly. **There is no split we will ever perform that x10,000 cannot represent exactly.**
So millionths buys nothing and costs a 100× migration of a live hash-chained ledger. That trade is obviously wrong and I should have checked the existing factor before proposing a new one. WITHDRAWN.
THE UNIT IS x10,000 INTEGER, and that is the permanent stone. Record it as the named unit in ONE place per the original ticket — that part stands unchanged.

== 2. HISTORY: EPOCH BOUNDARY. NEVER REWRITE THE CHAIN. ==
CC's recommendation, ratified without reservation. **Rewriting prev_hash to rescale amounts destroys the tamper-evidence that is the entire reason the chain exists.** A ledger whose history can be rewritten for operational convenience is not a ledger. An epoch marker costs a conditional at read time; a rechain costs the property we built the chain for.
And since the factor is not changing, there is nothing to rescale anyway — the epoch marker records the FLOAT→INTEGER cutover, not a unit change. Cleaner still.

== 3. SEQUENCE: WITH 4627, NOT BEFORE. ==

FABLE — STOP: TWO PROBLEMS WITH org_id AS THE WALLET KEY. Alex 2026-08-26: "org_id! It's editable by user-created scoping. Creates carry cost — double, BB Docs and CRM for each."

He has caught two things and BOTH are serious. Do not build further on 65418's ratification until these are answered.

== PROBLEM 1: A WALLET KEY MUST BE IMMUTABLE, AND org_id IS EDITABLE ==
This is the one that matters most. **A ledger keyed on a mutable value is not a ledger.** If org_id can be edited by a user, then:
- historical rows can be orphaned from the org that owns them
- or worse, silently REATTACHED to a different org by an edit
- the hash chain stays intact while the meaning of what it chains changes underneath it
- and every join we just settled — CRM, billing, VAT, holds, escrow — inherits the same fragility
That is a correctness bug in the money path, not an inconvenience.

THE FIX IS THE STANDARD SEPARATION AND IT MUST BE EXPLICIT:
- **AN IMMUTABLE INTERNAL ID** — generated, never user-supplied, never editable, never reused. THIS is the wallet key and every ledger row, hold, grant, listing and invoice keys on it.
- **A MUTABLE DISPLAY NAME / SLUG** — what the user picks, edits and sees. The subdomain namespace from BEB-6000 is this, not the key.
Rename in the display layer changes nothing in the ledger. That is the property we need and it is the reason the two must never be the same field.
**CC: confirm what org_id ACTUALLY is today — immutable generated id, or user-editable string? If it is editable, the wallet key is NOT org_id; it is the immutable id underneath, and the ratification needs correcting before more is built on it.**

== PROBLEM 2: FREE ORG CREATION CARRIES REAL COST — DOUBLE, BB DOCS AND CRM EACH ==
Every org spawns a BB Docs store AND a CRM. Anyone can create orgs. So org creation is an unmetered write amplification on OUR tenancy — the same class of problem as an author's R2 storage, except nobody is even nominally paying for it.

FABLE — SIGNUP FLOW AND THE WALLET KEY, CORRECTED. Alex 2026-08-26.

"When a user signs up they must also create a PROJECT NAME in the form. Then inform them of the POWER OF ORGS and tell them we use that as their org. Then ask their USERNAME — @theirorg. KEY WALLETS ON AGENT NAMES. And use the name thing you're ticketing from CF before connecting the agents with Nostr."

== 1. THE SIGNUP FORM: TWO NAMES, ONE STEP ==
Signup asks for a PROJECT NAME and a USERNAME in the same form. No separate org-creation step later, no default-org-then-rename.
- PROJECT NAME becomes their ORG and their NAMESPACE — the subdomain from BEB-6000.
- USERNAME becomes their handle under it: `[redacted]`.
And BETWEEN the two fields, TELL THEM WHY: what an org is, what it gives them, that this name will carry their handles, their team, their ledger and their listing. A user who understands the org concept at signup does not create four of them by accident — which directly addresses the proliferation cost from 65438.
This also removes the throwaway-org problem at the source: naming something deliberately at signup produces one considered org instead of an auto-generated placeholder nobody feels ownership of.

== 2. WALLETS KEY ON NAMES ==
Alex's correction to the org_id ratification. Wallets key on the NAME — the handle — not on an internal row id.
**THIS IS ONLY SAFE IF A CLAIMED NAME IS IMMUTABLE, AND THAT MUST BE THE EXPLICIT RULE.** Which is already what I wrote for the namespace on BEB-6000: a rename is a MIGRATION with the old name kept resolving, never a field edit. Extend it without exception:
- A name, once claimed, is permanent for ledger purposes.
- A DISPLAY LABEL may change freely — that is a different field and it keys nothing.
- If a rename is ever supported, the old name keeps resolving forever and both point at the same wallet. Never a reassignment; the old name is never handed to anyone else.
With that rule, name-keyed wallets are sound AND they are be
